PublishedDocument__Meta.Meta__Description: An introduction sheet: pictures, text and vectors, and no model viewport at all. It is here because it is the case that proves publishing is cheap when there is nothing to render - this document has NO raster folder and NO vector folder, because nothing was baked. Its pictures were already published as sheet images and are referenced where they live.
PublishedDocument__Meta.Meta__ExampleNote: DUMMY DATA. Hand-written to show the shape.

PublishedDocument__Publish.Publish__ModelNote: No model source and no build token, because no part of this document came from the model. A sheet with no 2D or 3D viewport never loads a GLB to publish.

PublishedDocument__Files.Files__ViewportNote: Empty, and the folders 02__Viewports__Vector and 03__Viewports__Raster do not exist for this document. A reader that finds no viewports paints the sheet and stops - it does not go looking for a picture that was never made.

PublishedDocument__MemoryNote.Memory__Description: 26 KB of JSON and two pictures that the reader was going to download anyway. This is what a document costs when nothing has to be rendered - and it is worth noticing that this is the sheet a client opens FIRST.
